issues.description: The UML/problem description and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template's Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This naming mismatch is structural and can confuse students: if they implement SealSaloon according to the diagram or follow the solution, calls to stock.addToStockIngredients(...) will not compile against the template. Conversely, students who use addItem in SealSaloon will diverge from the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML/specification by renaming the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or add a wrapper method addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem. This preserves the intended API shown in the problem diagram and matches the solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement's class diagram and the solution implementation use Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to add a new StockIngredient to the stock, but the template Stock class defines this operation as addItem(StockIngredient). This inconsistent method name across problem-specification, template, and solution can confuse students who are expected to call or rely on addToStockIngredients when wiring SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and may not find the expected method in the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add an alias wrapper) so the template, problem statement (UML), and solution use the same identifier for adding StockIngredient objects to the Stock.
